headline: CENTCOM offers up to $20M reward for information on Iran's nuclear program (Rewards for Justice)'

fault_line: Snitch money or a real intelligence operation -- is Washington buying its way inside Iran's nuclear program, or signalling it already has sources?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT] CENTCOM posted on X late Friday that the US 'is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community, or the movement of any of the above' (Al Jazeera, Nov 7 03:53Z; AP via stuccimedia confirms the post is linked to the State Department's Rewards for Justice program). Issued the same night as the Qeshm strikes and Trump's confirmation of limited strikes on Iranian air defences. [PORTWATCH -- N/A] No shipping/chokepoint element.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct declared-tier publisher families: Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) + AP (T1 wire, via stuccimedia). Both report the same CENTCOM X post.
sections.why_matters: $20 million and a new life -- if you tell Washington where Iran's nuclear program hides. CENTCOM posted the bounty the same night it hit Qeshm.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP -- CENTCOM offers up to $20M reward for information on Iran's nuclear program (Rewards for Justice)

totw_analysis: Our read: $20 million and a new life -- if you tell Washington where Iran's nuclear program hides. CENTCOM posted the bounty the same night it hit Qeshm. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Snitch money or a real intelligence operation -- is Washington buying its way inside Iran's nuclear program, or signalling it already has sources?
